messages:
maria: Heads up — I merged a tiny deps PR (#2894) that updated orjson to 3.8.5 to silence a deprecation warning. main CI is red immediately after the merge on the macOS job. Link: https://ci.example.com/runs/3344

ci-bot: build failed — job runtime-unit-macos (run 3344) 
  status: failed
  logs: https://ci.example.com/runs/3344/logs

maria: error from the job looks like a binary import problem, not our code. excerpt:
```
ImportError: /opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.10.12/x64/lib/python3.10/site-packages/orjson.cpython-310-darwin.so: invalid ELF header
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:\nTraceback (most recent call last):
  File \"tests/test_serialization.py\", line 42, in test_orjson_roundtrip
    assert deserialize(serialize(obj)) == obj
ImportError: cannot import name 'orjson' from 'orjson' (/opt/hostedtoolcache/...)
```

\nkevin: ugh, that looks like an architecture mismatch — darwin wheel on linux runner or vice-versa. But job name says macOS. Did the wheel come from a linux build?

jonathan: I can reproduce locally on my M1 mac with python 3.10. pip install orjson==3.8.5 gives a wheel that fails to load. seems the uploaded wheel in our wheelhouse might be for linux/amd64.

kevin: can we just rerun the job first? sometimes transient storage issue.

ci-bot: rerun requested by kevin — job queued

ci-bot: rerun completed — still failing (same stack)

jonathan: my suspicion: the new version pulled a transitive wheel from our internal cache that doesn't match the runner arch. We bumped the dependency indirectly in the lockfile when regenerating.

maria: next steps? revert PR or pin older orjson?

kevin: quick mitigation — revert the lockfile change (revert PR) so main is green. then investigate why the wrong wheel ended up in the cache.

jonathan: if someone wants to try a bisect instead of revert:
```
# find first bad commit on main
git checkout main
git bisect start HEAD HEAD~12
git bisect run pytest tests/test_serialization.py::test_orjson_roundtrip -q
```
But bisect will be slow since each step runs tests.

sre-oncall: I'll take cache/network side — checking object storage artifacts and our wheelhouse retention. Might be a publish job that pushed the wrong wheel tag earlier today.

maria: OK I'll open an immediate revert PR for the lockfile bump and tag you all. After revert I can repro locally and work with SRE to fix the wheelhouse and republish correct macOS wheel.

kevin: thanks. if you need a quick pin instead of full revert, pin orjson==3.8.4 in pyproject and regen lock — that should be less invasive for a short fix.

maria: noted. I'll open revert now, and then follow up with a proper reproduction + postmortem. Sorry for the noise :\)

jonathan: sounds good — ping me if you want me to run the bisect or test builds locally.

sre-oncall: I found the publish job that ran earlier: artifacts/orjson/3.8.5/ and it looks like the mac wheel upload failed but we have a stale linux wheel at that path. Investigating how the uploader chose the artifact path. Will report back in this thread.
